segments.title: Chương 221: Người nổi tiếng nói năng phải cẩn trọng
segments.content:
Chapter 224: 0221 Celebrities Should Watch What They Say

"Stop teasing CEO Chen, everyone. Go look at this other forwarded post, it's about unpaid wages for migrant workers. Here's the link..."

Amid the countless jeers, someone suddenly posted a link, and its keywords immediately caught the attention of netizens.

The title of that forwarded post was: "Law School Student Discusses Migrant Workers Demanding Back Pay. Apart from Chen Guiliang, Everyone Else Was Beating Around the Bush."

Li Guoqin: "This is a matter of policy and law. We who run companies can't answer that. Besides, internet companies basically don't hire migrant workers."

Student G: "Do the companies of our fellow alumni provide the 'Five Insurances and One Fund' for their employees?"

Wang Zhidong: "My company is completely aboveboard. Let's have another question."

Student G: "Why are the others silent?"

Chen Guiliang: "Let me speak. Currently, the state only focuses on promoting the 'Three Insurances,' but ByteDance and Game Science already provide the 'Five Insurances' for their employees. The 'One Fund' isn't mandatory either, but we still contribute it for our employees. As of last autumn, my companies have fully implemented the Five Insurances and One Fund. I believe that employees are the foundation of a company. No matter what, we can't let our employees be wronged."

Student G: "Then what are your thoughts on withholding wages from migrant workers, CEO Chen?"

Chen Guiliang: "My father went to work in Yangcheng very early on. When he was subcontracting a small project, his partner ran off with the final payment, leaving a portion of the migrant workers' wages unpaid. My parents have been working ever since to pay back those overdue wages. It took them eight years to finally settle the wages they owed. Last year, they asked me for another sum of money to cover the interest on the overdue wages as well."

The entire hall burst into applause.

Chen Guiliang: "Right now, this issue relies entirely on conscience, because the punishments are not severe enough. Even if a boss is sued for withholding wages, at most they'll just have to pay them back. There aren't sufficient fines, let alone the revocation of their construction qualifications."

Student G: "Thank you. I am very satisfied with that answer."

This conversation was posted on the Tianya Forum, and the post became even more popular than the previous GDP topic.

"Holy crap! Even the state-owned enterprises where I live only offer the 'Three Insurances.' CEO Chen's two companies provide the Five Insurances and One Fund?"

"Say no more. I'm resigning immediately to apply for a job at CEO Chen's company."

"Chen Guiliang is such a conscientious entrepreneur!"

"I take back all the ridicule I directed at CEO Chen. If he likes GDP that much, just let him keep bragging. It's not like bragging is a crime anyway."

"Is that story about his parents real?"

"Of course it's real. The West China Metropolis Daily reported on it. Because of CEO Chen's family background, he was considered pretty well-off in the countryside. But because his dad got screwed over by his partner, his parents had to keep working to pay off the debt and couldn't come home for a whole eight years. When CEO Chen was in middle and high school, he couldn't even afford meat. Every meal was just vegetables."

"Haha, I know which 'certain place' that student was talking about."

"Where are you from, person above me?"

"We have a one-stop service here. Take a guess."

Over at Peking University, the event had already ended.

Li Guoqin spoke to Chen Guiliang in private, "Xiao Chen, you're still too young. That student just now was just trying to show off, deliberately asking sensitive questions. You didn't need to say so much."

Chen Guiliang laughed. "I'm a straightforward person, can't keep things bottled up inside. Haha, I just say whatever's on my mind."

Li Guoqin said, "Words like that can easily offend people. It's best to say less of them in the future."

Wang Zhidong glanced at Chen Guiliang a few times, a thoughtful look on his face. He felt that Chen Guiliang had done it on purpose.

In truth, Wang Zhidong had really misunderstood.

Chen Guiliang had no intention of creating hype for himself. He just said what was on his mind.

If he didn't dare to say anything, what kind of reincarnator would he be?

He always kept up with the news, and sometimes what he read made him want to curse.

He had been wanting to get it off his chest for a long time.

As a result, the higher-ups naturally paid close attention, ordering the company to settle the 800,000 yuan in unpaid wages.

Chen Guiliang, reincarnated from twenty years in the future, felt physically ill seeing this kind of news.

It even awakened memories of his past life as an undercover journalist!

But his few words had coincided with a certain case, completely detonating the related public opinion.

"Xiao Chen, I suggest you don't accept any interviews for a while. It's hard to extricate yourself once you get caught up in the crossfire of public opinion."

"Understood. Thank you for the reminder, sir."

Chen Guiliang hung up the phone, feeling a bit of a headache.

At the beginning of the year, a migrant worker surnamed Li was beaten to death by five people while demanding his wages. The autopsy report concluded: sudden death due to a sudden increase in cardiac load, ruling out death by external violent trauma.

His children dropped out of school, sold all the grain at home, and borrowed money from everywhere they could, simultaneously filing appeals and contacting the media.

The matter blew up.

Half a month ago, the results of a second autopsy were released: death was induced by the acute onset of a pre-existing heart condition, triggered by factors such as external trauma and emotional distress.

The five assailants were finally arrested in accordance with the law.

Chen Guiliang, who was trying hard to quit smoking, couldn't resist taking out a cigarette and lighting it.

He had just been reading the various comments from netizens. Discussing the facts of the matter was certainly fine, but quite a few people were instigating trouble, and some were even taking the opportunity to spread rumors and slander.

Chen Guiliang even saw many familiar IDs, all of whom would become major online commentators with skewed views in the future.

And somehow, Chen Guiliang had become the "leader" of this public discourse.

Damn it.

He felt terrible if he didn't speak up.

But he felt even worse being used by others after he spoke.

After finishing the cigarette in silence, Chen Guiliang disabled the comment section on his homepage. Some of the comments were just infuriating to look at!

His secretary, Hu Yuexia, was in the outer office, constantly answering the phone, "I'm sorry, CEO Chen is very busy and is not accepting interviews at this time."

Chen Guiliang felt very vexed, but the media was in a frenzy.

They heaped praise upon him, bestowing titles like "Conscientious Entrepreneur."

Some reporters even went through the trouble of traveling to his village to interview Chen Guiliang's parents, asking for details about them working to repay the overdue wages.

Chen Xinghua still remembered his son's instructions and refused to be photographed, answering, "It's only right and proper to pay your debts. What's there to talk about? My fellow villagers worked for me, so I ought to pay them their wages."

When the reporter pressed further, Chen Xinghua clammed up.

The reporter could only go interview other villagers.

On the skyscraper's rooftop.

Chen Guiliang stood inside the railing, gazing at the city.

It was another damn sandstorm day.

Xie Yang had his mask pulled down to his chin, a cigarette in his mouth as he puffed out smoke. "Everything about Beijing is great, except for this climate. It's truly miserable. When I retire, I'm definitely not spending my old age in Beijing."

Chen Guiliang said, "Do you know what your greatest strength is?"

Xie Yang flicked his hair coolly. "Is it that I'm handsome?"

"You're tight-lipped. You don't run your mouth," Chen Guiliang said.

Xie Yang said, "You didn't run your mouth either. What you said this time was excellent, a total success. Both print media and the internet are praising you."

"That's what makes it so dangerous. The higher you fly, the harder you fall," Chen Guiliang said. "The public loves to create idols, but they also love to smash them. Damn it, the Beijing News laid the praise on so thick this time. The article was so nauseating to read."

Xie Yang laughed. "Haha, you're a youth idol now."

Chen Guiliang said, "I plan to lie low for a while, just attend class and write my book obediently."

"You're not going to make public statements anymore?" Xie Yang asked.

"How is that possible? When I need to call someone out, I'll still do it. But I'll need to pay more attention to my wording and perspective." Chen Guiliang wasn't one to give up eating for fear of choking.

Xie Yang stubbed out his cigarette and pulled his mask back on. "We have a new competitor. It's even more difficult to deal with than Bishawo."

"Who is it?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Xie Yang said, "51.com. The founder used to work under Ma Yun, and he's also the guy behind the 2345 URL directory."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Isn't that a gaming community?"

"No," Xie Yang said. "Aside from the mobile microblog feature, its functions are identical to HaiNei.com. Its user base mainly comes from traffic directed by the 2345 directory, mostly young people working in big cities, as well as netizens from second and third-tier cities and below. I noticed it at the beginning of the year but didn't pay it much mind, as many such websites were popping up. But just two days ago, 51.com announced its registered users have broken one million."

Chen Guiliang was surprised. "With that user demographic, they're taking a grassroots approach."

For 51.com to break out from the large crowd of SNS websites, its strategy was truly unconventional.

Many of its users didn't even know how to use a search engine. Every time they went online, they would habitually use the 2345 directory, through which they were directed to 51.com, and then they'd have a great time on the site.

They had never even heard of Kaixin001 or HaiNei!

Xie Yang said, "What do you think about us acquiring 9991.com? That directory site is fast, and so far no venture capitalists have made a move."

"There's no need. That website is too scummy. Acquiring it would be bad for the company's image," Chen Guiliang said. "You're thinking of learning from 51.com and directing grassroots users from directory sites, right?"

Xie Yang nodded. "Right."

Chen Guiliang said, "We can just pay sites like hao123, 265, and 9991 a fee. Have them put HaiNei on their homepages."

"That works too," Xie Yang said.

Chen Guiliang tugged at his mask. "I'm heading to the library. I need to do some proper research and write the fifth volume of 'Those Happenings of the Ming Dynasty.' I can't be bothered to read online comments these days!"

(End of Chapter)
